# WW2 Dispatches

> The Second World War, told on the day it happened. Every day WW2 Dispatches posts what happened on this date during the war, from the road to war in the 1930s to the surrender in 1945, with real archival photographs and film, checked against sources. A Wraithlight Digital project.

Posts run across four series: Battle Lines (battles and military operations), Home Front (civilian life), Blueprint (engineering and invention), and Statecraft (politics and diplomacy). Campaign Series follow one campaign on its real dates, told two ways: Day by Day (a short post each morning) and The Chronicle (the full account in three or four long parts).

## Main pages

- [About WW2 Dispatches](https://ww2dispatches.com/about): what the site is, what it posts and when, and how every dispatch is checked
- [Today's dispatches](https://ww2dispatches.com/): the home page, with the day's posts
- [On this day](https://ww2dispatches.com/on-this-day/): every daily dispatch, filed by calendar date, each on its own page with its sources
- [The Campaign Shelf](https://ww2dispatches.com/campaign-series/): every Campaign Series, each a book with Day by Day and The Chronicle
- [Name This](https://ww2dispatches.com/name-this/): a mystery WW2 photo twice a week, with every closed case and its answer
- [The Weekly Dispatch](https://ww2dispatches.com/newsletter/): one story from that week in the war, told in full, every Sunday
- [Declass](https://ww2dispatches.com/declass): the daily WW2 card game
- [Support WW2 Dispatches](https://ww2dispatches.com/support): a one time gift through Stripe; everything stays free to read

## Campaign Series

- [Pearl Harbor, 26 Nov to 8 Dec 1941](https://ww2dispatches.com/campaign-series/pearl-harbor-1941/): From the morning Japan's carriers slip out of the Kurils to the morning after the attack, when Roosevelt asks Congress for war.

## The Weekly Dispatch

- [No. 004: The Tide That Never Came](https://ww2dispatches.com/newsletter/004): A New Zealand officer who had lived beside Tarawa for fifteen years told the Marines there would not be three feet of water on the reef. On 20 November 1943 he was proved right, and thousands of men had to wade in under fire.
- [No. 003: Thirteen Minutes in Munich](https://ww2dispatches.com/newsletter/003): A quiet carpenter spent more than thirty nights alone inside a Munich beer hall, hollowing out the pillar behind Hitler's lectern. On 8 November 1939 his bomb went off just as he had planned. Hitler had walked out thirteen minutes earlier.
- [No. 002: The Spy Moscow Disowned](https://ww2dispatches.com/newsletter/002): Richard Sorge warned Stalin that Germany would invade, and was ignored. Then he told Moscow that Japan would not attack, and was believed. On 7 November 1944 Japan hanged him, and for twenty years the country he served would not admit he had been its spy.
- [No. 001: The Last Stand of Taffy 3](https://ww2dispatches.com/newsletter/001): On 25 October 1944, six little carriers and seven escorts woke up to find the biggest battleship ever built bearing down on them. This is what they did next.
